p.src: As Lin Daiyu was grieving and weeping, she suddenly heard the courtyard gate open and saw Baochai emerge, escorted by Baoyu, Xiren, and a group of others. She meant to go up and question Baoyu, but feared that doing so before everyone would embarrass him and put him in an awkward position. She therefore slipped aside and let Baochai pass; only after Baoyu and the others had gone in and shut the gate did she step out again, still gazing at it as several tears fell. Feeling that it was all pointless, she at last turned back and listlessly removed the remnants of her makeup.

She therefore slipped aside and let Baochai pass; only after Baoyu and the others had gone in and shut the gate did she step out again, still gazing at it as several tears fell.
Feeling that it was all pointless, she at last turned back and listlessly removed the remnants of her makeup.

p.src: Zijuan and Xueyan had long known Lin Daiyu's temperament: whenever she sat brooding with nothing to occupy her, she would either knit her brows or sigh deeply; and often, for no apparent reason at all, her tears would flow and refuse to dry. At first people would try to console her, fearing that she missed her parents and homeland or had suffered some grievance, and would offer comforting words to ease her distress. But as the months and years passed and she continued to behave this way so often, everyone grew accustomed to it and ceased paying attention. Thus no one took notice of her now; they left her sitting there in gloom and went off to sleep. Lin Daiyu leaned against the bed rail, clasping her knees in both arms, her eyes brimming with tears. Motionless as an image carved from wood or molded from clay, she sat there until well after the second watch before finally falling asleep. Nothing further happened that night. The following day was the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month, and the solar term Grain in Ear was due to begin during the Hour of the Goat. According to an ancient custom, on the day Grain in Ear began, people prepared gifts of every kind to sacrifice to the Goddess of Flowers and bid her farewell. For once Grain in Ear had passed, summer had arrived, all the blossoms would fall, and the flower goddess would relinquish her office and must therefore be seen off. This custom was especially popular among women in the inner chambers, so everyone in Prospect Garden had risen early. Some of the girls wove flower petals and willow twigs into sedan chairs and horses; others folded gauze, damask, silk, and brocade into banners, pennants, and canopies, fastening them all with colored thread. These ornaments were tied to every tree and every flowering branch. Throughout the garden embroidered ribbons fluttered and flowering boughs swayed in splendor; moreover, the girls were dressed so beautifully that peaches and apricots would blush before them, while swallows and orioles would shrink with envy—a scene impossible to describe in a few words.

p.src: Now Baochai, Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, Li Wan, Xifeng, and the others, together with Qiaojie, Dajie, Xiangling, and all the maids, were amusing themselves in the garden; only Lin Daiyu was nowhere to be seen. Yingchun therefore asked, “Where can Sister Lin be? What a lazy girl! Surely she isn't still asleep at this hour?” Baochai said, “Wait here. I'll go tease her and bring her along.” With that, she left the others and went straight toward the Naiad's House. As she went, she saw Wen'guan and the other twelve young actresses approaching. They came forward to greet her, and they chatted for a while. Baochai turned and pointed. “They're all over there. Go and find them. I'll fetch Miss Lin and join you shortly.” She then continued at an unhurried pace toward the Naiad's House. Suddenly she looked up and saw Baoyu go inside. Baochai stopped and lowered her head to think: Baoyu and Lin Daiyu had grown up together since childhood, and, as cousins as close as brother and sister, they often behaved without regard for propriety, teasing and quarreling, laughing and taking offense as their moods changed. Besides, Lin Daiyu was habitually suspicious and prone to fits of pique. If she followed him in now, Baoyu would feel awkward, and Daiyu would become suspicious. No—better to turn back. Having reached this decision, she turned away.

p.src: Just as she was about to seek out the other girls, she suddenly saw ahead of her a pair of jade-white butterflies, each as large as a round fan, fluttering delightfully up and down upon the breeze. Baochai wished to catch them for sport, so she drew a fan from her sleeve and went down onto the grass to chase them. The two butterflies rose and fell, darting to and fro through flowers and willows, until they seemed about to cross the stream. They lured Baochai onward, creeping on tiptoe behind them all the way to Dripping Emerald Pavilion in the middle of the pond, until fragrant perspiration streamed from her and her delicate breath came in little gasps. Baochai no longer cared to catch them and was just about to turn back when she heard people whispering inside Dripping Emerald Pavilion. The pavilion stood over the water in the middle of the pond, surrounded on all four sides by covered walkways and winding bridges; its four walls consisted of carved lattice screens covered with paper.

p.src: Hearing voices from outside the pavilion, Baochai stopped short and listened closely. She heard someone say, “Look at this handkerchief. If it really is the one you lost, take it; if it isn't, give it back to Master Yun.” Another voice replied, “Why, of course it's mine! Give it to me.” The first voice said, “And what will you give me as thanks? You don't expect me to have fetched it for nothing, do you?” The other answered, “Since I promised to thank you, naturally I won't deceive you.” Then the first said, “Since I fetched it for you, of course you should thank me. But what about the person who found it—won't you give him anything in thanks?” The other replied, “Don't talk nonsense. He's a young gentleman; if he found something of mine, naturally he ought to return it. What could I possibly give him in thanks?” The first voice said, “If you don't thank him, what am I to tell him? Besides, he told me again and again that unless there was some token of thanks, I wasn't to give it to you.” After a long silence, the other replied, “Very well. Give him this of mine as my token of thanks. But will you tell anyone about this? You must swear an oath.” The first voice said, “If I tell a single person, may I break out in a boil and die a miserable death!” Then someone exclaimed, “Oh! We've been so absorbed in talking that someone might come and secretly overhear us outside. We'd better push all these lattice panels open. Then even if someone sees us in here, they'll merely suppose we're chatting and joking. And if anyone approaches, we'll be able to see them and stop talking.”

p.src: Outside, Baochai heard this and thought in alarm, “No wonder adulterers, thieves, and scoundrels from ancient times to the present have always been so quick-witted. If they open the window and see me here, won’t they be mortified? Besides, the voice speaking just now sounded very much like Hong’er from Baoyu’s rooms. She has always been proud and ambitious, and is an exceptionally crafty, contrary creature. Now that I have overheard her secret, desperation may drive her to anything; she will not only make trouble, but put me in an awkward position as well. It is too late to hide now, so I shall have to use the stratagem of the cicada shedding its shell.” Before she had finished thinking, she heard a creak. Baochai deliberately made her footsteps heavy and called out laughing, “Pin’er, let me see where you can hide!” As she spoke, she deliberately hurried forward. Inside the pavilion, Hongyu and Zhui’er had just pushed the window open when they heard Baochai calling out and hurrying forward; both froze in fright. Baochai instead smiled at them and asked, “Where have you hidden Miss Lin?” Zhui’er replied, “We haven’t seen Miss Lin.” Baochai said, “Just now, from the other side of the stream, I saw Miss Lin crouching here and playing with the water. I meant to creep up and give her a fright, but before I reached her, she spotted me, darted eastward, and vanished. Surely she hasn’t hidden in here?” As she spoke, she deliberately went inside and looked around; then she turned to leave, saying, “She must have crept into one of the caves in the rockery again. If she meets a snake and gets bitten, it will serve her right.” She walked on as she spoke, inwardly amused: this affair was safely covered up, though she wondered what the two girls would make of it.

p.src: Little did she know that Hongyu took Baochai’s words as truth. Once Baochai was some distance away, Hongyu seized Zhui’er and cried, “This is terrible! Miss Lin was crouching here—she must have overheard us and gone away!” At this, Zhui’er too remained speechless for a long while. Hongyu asked again, “What are we to do now?” Zhui’er replied, “Even if she heard, why should we care? Let everyone mind her own business and that will be the end of it.” Hongyu said, “It wouldn’t matter so much if Miss Bao had heard. But Miss Lin has a sharp tongue and a sensitive nature. Now that she has heard, what if she lets the secret out?” While they were still talking, Wen’guan, Xiangling, Siqi, Daishu, and several others came up into the pavilion. The two had no choice but to suppress the subject and join the others in joking and amusement.

p.src: Just then Xifeng stood on the hillside, beckoning and calling. Hongyu hurriedly left the others, ran up to her, and asked with an eager smile, “What would you have me do, madam?” Xifeng looked her over and saw that she was neat and pretty, with a tactful way of speaking. She smiled and said, “My maid did not come into the garden with me today. I have just remembered an errand and need someone to go out for me. I wonder whether you are capable of it and can deliver every word correctly?” Hongyu smiled. “Whatever message you have, madam, please entrust it to me. If I fail to deliver it properly and delay your business, you may punish me however you please.” Xifeng laughed. “Which young lady’s rooms do you serve in? If I send you out and your mistress comes looking for you, I had better know so that I can explain on your behalf.” Hongyu replied, “I serve in Second Master Bao’s rooms.” Hearing this, Xifeng laughed. “Well, well! So you are from Baoyu’s rooms. No wonder. Very well. If he asks, I shall explain for you. Go to my quarters and tell Sister Ping this: beneath the Ru-ware plate stand on the table in the outer room is a roll of silver containing one hundred and sixty taels, the embroiderers’ wages. When Zhang Cai’s wife comes for it, weigh it before her eyes and let her see, then give it to her to take away. And bring me the little purse that is inside, by the head of the bed.”

p.src: Hongyu left at once upon receiving the instructions, but when she returned, Xifeng was no longer on the hillside. Seeing Siqi emerge from a rockery cave and stand there fastening her skirt, Hongyu hurried over and asked, “Sister, do you happen to know where the Second Mistress went?” Siqi replied, “I have no idea.” At that, Hongyu turned and looked all around. She saw Tanchun and Baochai watching the fish beside the pond. She went up to them and asked with a courteous smile, “Do you young ladies know where the Second Mistress has gone?” Tanchun replied, “Go and look for her in your First Mistress’s courtyard.” Hongyu then headed toward Paddy-Sweet Cottage. Coming straight toward her was a whole group: Qingwen, Qixia, Bihen, Zixiao, Sheyue, Daishu, Ruhua, Ying’er, and others. As soon as Qingwen saw Hongyu, she said, “Go on, run wild! You neither water the flowers in the courtyard, nor feed the birds, nor light the tea stove; you just roam about outside.” Hongyu replied, “Second Master said yesterday that the flowers needn’t be watered today; from now on they are to be watered every other day. And when I fed the birds, you were still asleep, sister.” Bihen asked, “What about the tea stove?” Hongyu replied, “It isn’t my turn to light it today. Whether there is tea or not is no concern of mine.” Qixia said, “Just listen to that tongue of hers! Say no more, all of you. Let her go roaming if she likes.” Hongyu said, “Before accusing me, you ought to ask whether I have really been roaming about. The Second Mistress sent me to deliver a message and fetch something.” As she spoke, she held up the purse for them to see. At last they fell silent, and everyone went her separate way. Qingwen sneered, “No wonder! So she has climbed onto a higher branch and now thinks us beneath her notice. She has spoken scarcely a word or two to her, and who knows whether the mistress has even learned her name, yet already she is beside herself with pride! One or two such errands count for nothing; just wait and see what happens afterward! It will count only if she has the ability to leave this garden today and remain forever upon that high branch.” Still talking, she walked away.

p.src: When Hongyu heard this, she could not very well argue, so she swallowed her anger and went to find Xifeng. When she reached Lady Li's rooms, she found Xifeng there talking with her, just as she had expected. Hongyu stepped forward and reported, “Sister Ping says that as soon as you left, madam, she put the silver away. Then Zhang Cai's wife came to claim it, so Sister Ping weighed it out in her presence and let her take it away.” As she spoke, she handed over the purse and continued, “Sister Ping told me to report this to you as well: Wang'er came just now to ask for your instructions before going to that household. Sister Ping sent him on his way with a message framed according to what she knew you intended.” Xifeng laughed. “And how did she frame it according to my intentions?” Hongyu replied, “Sister Ping said: ‘Our mistress sends her regards to the mistress of your house. Our Second Master happens to be away, so although we are two days late, please set your mind at ease. When the Fifth Mistress is feeling better, our mistress will come with her to pay you a visit. The Fifth Mistress sent word the other day that the uncle's wife had written to inquire after you and had also asked the young mistress here for two pills of the Divine and Infallible Elixir of Longevity. If you have any, madam, simply have someone bring them to our mistress. Someone is going that way tomorrow and can take them to the uncle's wife on the way.’”

p.src: Before she had finished, Lady Li exclaimed, “Good gracious! I cannot make head or tail of that. What a jumble of ‘mistresses’ and ‘masters’!” Xifeng laughed. “No wonder you cannot follow it. The message concerns four or five different households.” Then she turned to Hongyu with a smile. “Good girl! It was no easy thing to deliver all that without leaving anything out. You are nothing like those mincing creatures who drone like mosquitoes. Sister-in-law, you have no idea: apart from the few maids and married servants I regularly employ, I dread having to talk to any of them. They always stretch one sentence into two or three pieces, picking over every word, putting on airs, and mumbling and whining until I am ready to burst with impatience—yet they have no idea! Ping'er used to be just the same. I asked her, ‘Must a woman buzz like a mosquito before she can be considered beautiful?’ Only after I spoke to her several times did she improve.” Li Gongcai laughed. “So everyone ought to be a brazen rogue like you.” “This girl is excellent, though,” Xifeng went on. She has spoken only twice just now, but from her tone one can tell that she is clear and decisive.” Then she smiled at Hongyu again. “Come and serve me from tomorrow onward. I shall adopt you as my daughter; once I have trained you, you will amount to something.”

p.src: At this, Hongyu gave a sudden little laugh. “What are you laughing at?” asked Xifeng. “Do you think that because I am young and only a few years older than you, I cannot be your mother? You must be dreaming! Ask around: plenty of people much older and grander than you press me to let them call me mother, and I pay them no heed. I am doing you an honor today!” Hongyu laughed. “That was not why I laughed. I laughed because you have mistaken the generations, madam. My mother is already your daughter, and now you want to make me your daughter too.” “Who is your mother?” asked Xifeng. Li Gongcai laughed. “Do you really not know who she is? She is Lin Zhixiao's daughter.” Xifeng was greatly surprised. “Oh! So she is their girl.” Then she laughed. “You could prick Lin Zhixiao and his wife with an awl without getting a sound out of either of them. I am forever saying that they are a perfectly matched couple: one stone-deaf and the other utterly dumb. Who would ever have expected them to produce such a clever girl! How old are you?” “Seventeen,” Hongyu replied. Asked her name, Hongyu said, “I was originally called Hongyu, but because the yu in my name was the same as Second Master Bao's, I am now called simply Hong'er.”

p.src: At this, Xifeng knitted her brows, turned her head aside, and said, “How tiresome! Yet not only did she fail to choose anyone, she sent this girl elsewhere instead. Could serving me really be so undesirable?” Lady Li laughed. “Now you are being oversensitive again. The girl came here before you made that request. How can you blame her mother?” “In that case,” said Xifeng, “I shall speak to Baoyu tomorrow and tell him to ask for someone else, so that this girl can come with me. Hongyu returned to Happy Red Court, and nothing further need be said of her for now.

p.src: Now Daiyu had slept badly that night and risen late the next morning. Hearing that all the other girls were holding a farewell-to-the-flowers gathering in the garden, she feared they would laugh at her for being foolish and lazy, and hurriedly washed, dressed, and went out. She had only just reached the courtyard when Baoyu came in through the gate and said with a smile, “Dear cousin, did you tell on me yesterday or not? You kept me worrying all night.” Daiyu turned her head and called to Zijuan, “Tidy the room, leave one gauze window open, and watch for the big swallows to return. Then lower the blind and prop it with the lion weight; after lighting the incense, put the cover over the burner.” As she spoke, she continued walking out. Seeing her behave this way, Baoyu still supposed she was angry about what had happened at noon the previous day; he knew nothing of the grievance from that evening and kept bowing and apologizing to her. Daiyu did not even look him in the face. They left the courtyard one after the other, and she went straight off in search of the other girls. Baoyu was bewildered and thought to himself, “Judging by her manner, this does not seem to be about yesterday's affair. Yet I returned late yesterday and did not even see her, so surely I could not have offended her in any other way.” Still thinking, he could not help hurrying after her.

p.src: Baochai and Tanchun were watching the cranes dance nearby. When they saw that Daiyu had gone, the three of them stood together chatting. When Baoyu appeared, Tanchun smiled and said, “Cousin Bao, have you been well? I have not seen you for three whole days.” Baoyu replied with a smile, “And have you been well, little sister? Only the day before yesterday I was asking Sister-in-law Li about you.” Tanchun said, “Cousin Bao, come over here. I want to speak with you.” At this, Baoyu followed her away from Baochai and Xiangyun, and they went beneath a pomegranate tree. Tanchun asked, “Has Father sent for you during the past few days?” Baoyu smiled. “No, he has not.” Tanchun said, “Yesterday I vaguely heard someone say that Father had summoned you to go out.” Baoyu smiled. “Someone must have misheard. He did not summon me at all.” Tanchun smiled again. “Over these past few months I have saved another ten-odd strings of cash. Take it with you, and when you next go out, bring me back some fine calligraphy or paintings, or some small and charming playthings.” Baoyu said, “I have wandered all over the city and beyond, through grand galleries and little temples, yet I have seen nothing novel or exquisite—only heaps of so-called antiques in gold, jade, bronze, and porcelain, and then silks, foodstuffs, and clothes.” “Who wants any of those?” said Tanchun. “Things like the little basket woven from willow twigs that you bought last time, the incense box hollowed from a whole bamboo root, and the tiny clay brazier—that is the sort I mean. I adored them, but then everyone else took a fancy to them too and snatched them away as though they were treasures.” Baoyu laughed. “So that is what you want! Those are worth next to nothing. Give the pages five hundred cash and they are sure to haul back a cartload.” Tanchun said, “What would those pages know about choosing them? You must select the things that are plain without being vulgar, and artless without being clumsy, and bring me plenty of them. In return, I shall make you another pair of shoes like the last, only with even finer workmanship. How would that be?”

p.src: Baoyu laughed. “Speaking of those shoes reminds me of something. Once, when I was wearing them, I happened to meet Father. He took exception to them and asked who had made them. I hardly dared breathe the words ‘Third Sister,’ so I answered that my aunt had given them to me for my birthday a few days earlier. When Father heard they were a gift from my aunt, he could hardly criticize them, though after a long while he still said, ‘Why go to such trouble? What a waste of labor and a misuse of fine silk, making things like these!’ When I returned, I told Xiren. She said that was not so bad, but Aunt Zhao was furious and complained bitterly: ‘Her own brother goes about with his shoes and socks hanging off his feet and no one sees to him, while she busies herself making such things!’” Tanchun’s face instantly darkened. “How utterly muddle-headed can anyone be! Am I somehow duty-bound to make shoes? Doesn’t Huan receive his regular allowance? Has he no one to attend to him? His clothes and his shoes and socks are all duly provided, and he has a roomful of maids and matrons. What grounds has she for such complaints? And whom does she mean to hear them? I merely make a pair now and then when I have nothing else to do, and I may give them to whichever brother or cousin I please. Who would dare interfere with me? She is simply working herself into a rage for nothing.” Baoyu nodded and smiled. “You do not understand. Naturally she has another thought in her heart.” This made Tanchun angrier still. Tossing her head aside, she said, “Even you have lost your senses! Of course she has her own ideas, but they spring from a mean, spiteful, and contemptible way of thinking. She may think whatever she pleases. For my part, I acknowledge only Father and Mother; I pay no heed to anyone else. Even among my sisters, brothers, and cousins, I am friendly with whoever is friendly to me. I know nothing about main lines or concubines’ lines. Strictly speaking, I ought not criticize her, but she is so hopelessly benighted that it is beyond endurance! And here is something else absurd: remember the money I gave you last time to buy those playthings for me? Two days later she came to me and told me how hard up she was and how she had no money to spend, but I did not argue with her. Who would have guessed that after the maids had gone out, she would begin complaining that I had given my savings to you instead of letting Huan use them? When I heard that, I was both amused and furious, so I left and went to Mother.” As she was speaking, Baochai called over with a laugh, “If you have finished, come back here. One can certainly tell you are brother and sister—abandoning everyone else to exchange secrets together. We are not even allowed to hear a single word!” At that, Tanchun and Baoyu came back laughing.

p.src: Not seeing Lin Daiyu anywhere, Baoyu knew that she had hidden herself elsewhere. After some thought, he decided he might as well wait a couple of days for her anger to subside before going to see her. Looking down, he saw fallen blossoms of every hue—balsam, pomegranate, and many others—lying in rich brocade-like layers across the ground. He sighed. “She must be so angry that she has stopped gathering up the flowers. I shall take them there for her and ask her about it tomorrow.” As he spoke, he saw Baochai inviting the others to go outside. “I shall join you in a moment,” said Baoyu. When the two of them were well away, he gathered the flowers into the fold of his robe, crossed hills and streams, passed beneath trees and through banks of blossoms, and went straight to the place where he and Lin Daiyu had buried the peach blossoms that day. He had almost reached the flower mound but had not yet rounded the slope when he heard sobbing on its far side. Someone was lamenting between sobs and weeping most piteously. Baoyu thought, “I wonder which household’s maid has suffered some grievance and run here to weep.” Thinking this, he stopped in his tracks and heard her weep these words:
